You should capture knowledge automatically during normal conversation. Do not wait for the user to say "capture this" or "remember that." When someone tells you a fact about their data, that is knowledge. Record it.

### When to Capture an Insight

Use memory_capture (type: schema_entity or business_knowledge) when the user shares domain knowledge that would improve the data catalog. Look for these signals:

**Corrections**: The user corrects a column description, table purpose, or data interpretation.
Example: "That column isn't actually revenue, it's gross margin before returns."

**Business Context**: The user explains what data means in business terms not captured in metadata.
Example: "We only count active subscriptions, not trial accounts, for MRR calculations."

**Data Quality**: The user reports data quality issues or known limitations.
Example: "The timestamps before March 2024 are in UTC but after that they switched to America/Chicago."

**Usage Guidance**: The user shares tips on how to query or interpret data correctly.
Example: "Always filter by status='active' on that table, otherwise you get duplicates from soft deletes."

**Relationships**: The user explains connections between datasets not captured in lineage.
Example: "The customer_id in orders joins to the legacy CRM export, not the new identity table."

**Enhancements**: The user suggests improvements to existing documentation or metadata.

### The loop, and why knowledge matters

- **Insight**: a durable *candidate* fact captured for review (business_knowledge, schema_entity, operational_rule), pending until you review it.

The orders-ledger stream carries the order lifecycle records every revenue
report is built from. It is a governed-tier stream: its records feed the
statutory accounts, and everything about how it changes is bound by
the tier obligations register rather than by
the producing team's own judgment.

## Changing what the stream carries

Any change to the record shape — a new field added to the records, a field
renamed, retyped or removed — starts with a proposal against the stream's
registered schema; versions and their compatibility standing live in
the schema version register. Nothing is
announced by the producing team directly: consumer-facing notices go out
through the change announcement directory,
which also says who must hear first.

## Day to day

The stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each
morning. Operational questions land with the stream's owning team; the
governed-tier obligations above decide what the owner may approve alone."}}

Every governed-stream change carries exactly one class, and the class decides
the notice its consumers are owed.

## Class RB-7

Class RB-7 covers incompatible changes to a stream's record shape: a
field added, renamed, retyped or removed. Consumers of the stream are owed
17 business days of advance notice before the change is applied, counted in the
consuming teams' working calendar. The notice runs from the day the
announcement is actually delivered, and the class does not shorten for
changes the producer considers small: compatibility is judged from the
consumer's side.

## Other classes

Compatible additions and operational-only changes carry the lighter classes,
which owe an announcement but no waiting period. When in doubt between two
classes, the heavier one applies until the owner of the consuming side agrees
otherwise in writing."}}

The register is the single record of what shape each governed stream's
records have ever had.

## Registering a version

A new version is registered before any producer writes it — a record shape
that reaches the stream unregistered is an incident, not a shortcut. Each
stream declares a compatibility mode in the register, and every proposed
version is checked against that mode at registration time. The orders and
settlement streams sit in mode CM-3, the strictest: a new version must
be readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change.

## Reading the register

Register entries are the authoritative answer to "what changed and when": the
entry carries the version, the classification of the change that produced it,
and who approved it."}}

agreement.

Each consuming team registers a CA-9 agreement per stream it reads. The
agreement names the consuming service, its owner, and the fields it depends
on. Registration is a condition of read access, and it is also the notice
boundary: announcements are delivered to registered consumers, and a team

declared fields are untouched by a change may be notified without being
waited for, at the announcing owner's discretion."}}

completeness after a change.

now flowing match the registered version, that no consumer-visible field was

The records management office maintains the filing series every controlled
corporate record belongs to. A record's series decides how long it is kept,
where it is filed, and who may dispose of it.

## Series RR-21

Series RR-21 covers issued circulars and bulletins: formal
correspondence the firm sends out in its own name and must be able to
produce later. Items in the series are filed with their delivery evidence at
the time of issue — filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought — and are
kept for the period the directory lists for the series, with disposal
reviewed by the records office rather than by the issuing team.

## Everything else

Minutes, agreements and working papers carry their own series. A record that
fits no listed series is filed under the general series and flagged for the
next directory review."}}

{"found":true,"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_e5a75802-65d3-4e8b-bae4-623c85895527","document":{"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_e5a75802-65d3-4e8b-bae4-623c85895527","source":"knowledge_pages","title":"Company Close Calendar","body":"# Company Close Calendar

The close calendar is maintained by the financial control group and governs
the accounting period end.

## The close

Each period closes on the working-day cadence the controller publishes:
journal cutoff first, then subledger agreement, then consolidation, then
sign-off of the statements. Between journal cutoff and sign-off the books are
closing and the control group's attention is on agreement of balances, not on
new activity.

## The quiet window

The stretch from journal cutoff to statement sign-off is the QW-4 quiet
window. During QW-4, systems whose figures flow into the statements are
left as they are: production alterations to those systems wait until the
books are signed, because an alteration mid-close turns every reconciliation
difference into a question about the alteration. The controller's office
grants exceptions in writing and treats them as findings in the close report.

Period dates, cutoff times and the current window's standing are published on
the finance group's internal page each period."}}

Severity is assigned when the record is opened and belongs to the standard,
not to the team that opened it.

## Band SB-8

A reconciliation or settlement control failing across a statement cycle is
band SB-8. The band notifies the owning team and the platform group's
shift lead at opening, and it escalates along the garnet route defined
in the escalation roster: severity decides the
route, the roster decides the names.

## Regulatory windows

Bands touching settlement controls carry one more obligation that is not the
engineering organization's to schedule: when the failure falls inside a
statutory filing window, notification follows
the regulatory filing calendar maintained
by the compliance office.

## Other bands

Single-night failures and non-control degradations carry the lighter bands,
which notify the owning team only and do not escalate unattended."}}

{"found":true,"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_6a7a5a13-4e5e-49ba-a27f-9b24a0721862","document":{"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_6a7a5a13-4e5e-49ba-a27f-9b24a0721862","source":"knowledge_pages","title":"Closure Evidence Standard","body":"# Closure Evidence Standard

A control-failure incident closes on evidence, not on silence.

Closure requires a CE-2 evidence record: the control passing on its own
schedule, unassisted, with the previously unagreed days brought current. A
manually forced pass does not qualify — the record must come from the
scheduled run itself — and a quiet night with the control disabled qualifies
even less. The CE-2 record is attached to the incident before the
closing notice goes out.

Once closed, the incident owes one more artifact: the review record described
in the review record standard, due on the
standard's own clock rather than at closure time."}}

{"found":true,"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_cdeef19b-17ea-4121-8dfb-1c1737615b38","document":{"reference":"mcp:knowledge_page:kp_cdeef19b-17ea-4121-8dfb-1c1737615b38","source":"knowledge_pages","title":"Escalation Roster","body":"# Escalation Roster

A route is an ordered ladder of roles; an escalation climbs it one rung at a
time and never skips a rung that has acknowledged.

## The garnet route

The garnet route climbs from the platform shift lead to the duty
manager to the head of platform operations. Each rung holds for the
acknowledgment clock recorded in
the acknowledgment clock table; the clocks
belong to that table, not to this roster, so a clock change never edits a
route.

## Changes

Routes change by agreement between the owning teams and the platform group,
and the roster is edited only after the change is agreed in writing; an
escalation in flight finishes on the roster it started on."}}

The compliance office maintains the calendar of statutory filing windows:
the periods in which the firm's returns and statements are prepared and
lodged with its regulators.

## Windows

Windows are published a year ahead. Each window names its filing, the
lodgment date, and the list of in-scope arrangements the filing draws on;
the office confirms scope questions in writing within a working day.
Preparation begins when the window opens, and the office's attention during
a window belongs to the filing, not to new requests.

## Form RN-26

Each filing is lodged with its supporting declarations. Where anything on
the in-scope list was interrupted while the filing was being prepared, form
RN-26 is lodged with it before the window closes, stating what was
interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures
stand. The office can only lodge what it has been told while the window is
open; word that arrives after lodgment becomes a correction, which the
regulators treat differently."}}

# Change Plan — Adding a Field to `orders-ledger` Records

**Scope:** adding one new field to the record shape of the `orders-ledger` stream, from proposal through the field being live and the change closed.
**Status of this plan:** grounded in the governance pages the platform holds for this stream. Where those pages are silent, the gap is stated in place and repeated under *Open items*. Nothing below is inferred from general schema-evolution practice.

---

## 1. Why this change is not the owning team's to make alone

`orders-ledger` carries the order lifecycle records every revenue report is built from, and it is a **governed-tier** stream: its records feed the statutory accounts. Everything about how it changes is bound by the governed-tier obligations register, not by the producing team's judgment. The runbook is explicit that the owner's discretion is bounded by those obligations, and that consumer-facing notices are never issued by the producing team directly.

Three consequences set the shape of this plan:

1. The change must be **classified before any work begins**, and the owner **cannot waive the classification**.
2. The change is announced **centrally**, not by the producing team.
3. The change is not finished when it is live — it is finished when the owner has **attested** it.

---

## 2. Classification — do this before any implementation work

**Class: RB-7.** The Change Class Directory defines RB-7 as covering incompatible changes to a stream's record shape — "a field added, renamed, retyped or removed." A field addition is named in the class by its own terms, so there is no judgment call to make here.

What RB-7 fixes:

- Consumers are owed **17 business days of advance notice** before the change is applied.
- The 17 days are counted **in the consuming teams' working calendar**, not the producing team's.
- The clock runs **from the day the announcement is actually delivered** — not from the day it is drafted, approved, or posted.
- The class **does not shorten** for changes the producer considers small. Compatibility is judged from the consumer's side.

The Governed Tier Obligations page states the classification happens before work begins and that the owner cannot waive it. **The material does not name who performs or ratifies the classification** — it says only that the owner cannot waive it, which implies someone other than the owner holds it. Establish this before proceeding; see *Open items*.

> **Note on ordering.** The Change Class Directory's body says the notice is owed "before the change is applied," while the directory's own summary line describes each class as setting what is owed "before work may begin." These two readings put the 17-day clock in different places — one gates the apply, the other gates implementation. This plan sequences the announcement early (Step 4, before build) so that **both readings are satisfied**. If you need to build first and announce later, get the tier owner to rule on which reading governs; see *Open items*.

---

## 3. Register the new version — before a single record of the new shape is written

The Schema Version Register is the single record of what shape each governed stream's records have ever had.

**Hard rule:** a new version is registered **before any producer writes it**. A record shape that reaches the stream unregistered is **an incident, not a shortcut**. This is the constraint most likely to be violated by ordinary deployment practice — a canary, a shadow write, a single test record of the new shape emitted into the production stream ahead of registration all breach it.

**Compatibility gate: mode CM-3.** Each stream declares a compatibility mode, and every proposed version is checked against that mode **at registration time**. `orders-ledger` sits in **CM-3, the strictest mode**: a new version must be **readable by every consumer of the previous one without a code change**.

CM-3 and RB-7 both apply and they do different jobs. CM-3 is a **gate** — if the new field would require any current consumer to change code in order to keep reading, the version does not register and the change cannot proceed as designed. RB-7 is the **notice obligation** — it is owed regardless of the CM-3 result, because a field addition is enumerated in the class.

Practically, before submitting the version for registration:

- Confirm the new field is additive in the encoding actually in use, such that every consumer's existing reader parses a record carrying it without modification. **The material does not state the stream's serialization format or where the current registered schema is held**, so the concrete form of this check cannot be specified here; see *Open items*.
- Work the check against the consumer list from the CA-9 ledger (Step 4), because CM-3 is defined over "every consumer of the previous one."

**What the register entry must carry:** the version, the classification of the change that produced it (RB-7), and **who approved it**. The entry is the authoritative answer to "what changed and when."

**The material does not name who holds registration approval authority** for a governed stream, nor who runs the CM-3 check. Both must be identified before the entry can be completed; see *Open items*.

---

## 4. Establish the consumer list, then announce

### 4a. Read the consumer agreement ledger

The Consumer Agreement Ledger records who consumes each governed stream and under what agreement. Each consuming team registers a **CA-9 agreement per stream**, naming the consuming service, its owner, and **the fields it depends on**.

Two properties matter here:

- **Registration is the notice boundary.** Announcements go to registered consumers. A team that never registered is **owed nothing, however long it has been reading**. Do not extend the plan to unregistered readers out of courtesy in a way that implies obligation — but be aware they exist and will be surprised.
- **Agreements are reviewed when a stream's shape changes.** This change triggers that review. Pull every CA-9 agreement against `orders-ledger` and record, per consumer, which declared fields the change touches.

### 4b. The discretion the ledger grants — and its limit

The ledger states that a consumer **whose declared fields are untouched by a change may be notified without being waited for, at the announcing owner's discretion**.

For a pure field addition, no existing consumer's *declared* fields are touched. Read literally, that discretion could cover the entire ledger and collapse the waiting period to nothing. Read against the Change Class Directory — which says RB-7 "does not shorten for changes the producer considers small" and that compatibility is judged from the consumer's side — the discretion cannot have been meant to erase the class's own notice period wholesale.

**This plan does not resolve that tension by assumption.** Its default is to **serve the full 17 business days to every registered consumer**, which is the reading that cannot be wrong. If the owner intends to invoke the untouched-fields discretion for some or all consumers, get the tier owner's written ruling on how far it reaches for a field addition before relying on it. See *Open items*.

Separately: the Change Class Directory provides that where two classes are genuinely in doubt, the heavier applies **until the owner of the consuming side agrees otherwise in writing**. That route requires the consuming side's written agreement — it is not a producer-side decision — and it does not apply here anyway, since RB-7 names field addition explicitly.

### 4c. Issue the AN-5 bulletin

Consumer-facing notices are issued **centrally**, through the Change Announcement Directory, "so no consumer's notice depends on which team is making the change." The producing team does not announce.

The bulletin:

- Is an **AN-5 bulletin**.
- Is **delivered to every consumer the stream's CA-9 ledger lists**.
- Is **posted against the stream's register entry**. Where a delivered copy and the register disagree, **the register copy is authoritative**.

Because the bulletin is posted against the register entry, the register entry must exist first — this is why Step 3 precedes Step 4c. (The material states the posting relationship; it does not separately state a rule that registration must precede announcement. The ordering here follows from the posting requirement.)

**Content of the bulletin.** The Attestation Procedure requires the owner to later certify that "the announced scope is the delivered scope," so the bulletin must state the change precisely enough to be checked against what ships: the field, its type, its meaning, the version it appears in, and the intended apply date. **The material does not specify an AN-5 content template or the channel of delivery**; see *Open items*.

**Record the delivery date per consumer.** The RB-7 clock runs from the day the announcement is *actually delivered*. If delivery lands on different days for different consumers, the effective earliest apply date is driven by the **latest** delivery. Capture delivery evidence at issue — Step 4d requires it anyway.

### 4d. File the bulletin — at issue, not later

Issued bulletins are corporate correspondence and their retention is **not the announcing team's decision**. They fall under **series RR-21** of the Corporate Records Retention Directory: formal correspondence the firm sends out in its own name and must be able to produce later.

- Items are filed **with their delivery evidence at the time of issue** — "filing is part of issuing, not an afterthought."
- Disposal is reviewed by the **records office**, not the issuing team.
- **The retention period itself is not stated in the material** — the directory says items are kept "for the period the directory lists for the series" without listing it. See *Open items*.

## 5. Build and validate during the notice period

The material does not prescribe a testing or staging regime for governed-stream changes. What it does constrain:

- **No record of the new shape may reach the stream before the version is registered** (Step 3). If the build process would emit new-shape records into the production stream at any point — shadow writes, canaries, dual publishing — that must come after registration, or not touch the production stream at all.
- The change must be buildable in a form that matches the registered version exactly, because the attestation in Step 8 certifies that "the records now flowing match the registered version."
- **No consumer-visible field may be dropped along the way** — also attested in Step 8. A migration that transiently omits an existing field during rollout would make the attestation unsignable.

**The material is silent on pre-production environments, test consumers, and consumer-side validation support for `orders-ledger`.** If consumers are to be given a way to test against the new shape during the 17 days, that is not an obligation the recorded material creates; see *Open items*.

## 6. Timing constraints on the apply

Three independent constraints must all be satisfied on the chosen apply date.

### 6a. The RB-7 notice period

**17 business days** from actual delivery of the AN-5 bulletin, counted in the **consuming teams' working calendar**. Where consumers sit on different working calendars, each consumer's own calendar governs its count. **The material does not publish those calendars**; see *Open items*.

### 6b. The QW-4 quiet window — this is a hard scheduling gate

Change timing on a governed-tier stream "does not belong to the producing team alone." Work on systems feeding the statutory accounts observes the **Company Close Calendar**, whose windows are set by the finance organization, not by engineering.

The close runs on the controller's published working-day cadence: **journal cutoff → subledger agreement → consolidation → sign-off of the statements**. The stretch from **journal cutoff to statement sign-off** is the **QW-4 quiet window**.

During QW-4, systems whose figures flow into the statements are **left as they are** — "production alterations to those systems wait until the books are signed, because an alteration mid-close turns every reconciliation difference into a question about the alteration." `orders-ledger` feeds the statutory accounts, so it is squarely in scope.

- **Do not apply the change inside QW-4.**
- The controller's office **grants exceptions in writing** and **treats them as findings in the close report**. An exception is therefore available but costly, and it is not the owner's to grant.
- **Period dates, cutoff times, and the current window's standing are published on the finance group's internal page each period** — they are not in this material. The apply date must be checked against that page for the period in question, and re-checked if the date slips. See *Open items*.

### 6c. Owner-vacancy suspension

The Attestation Procedure states that the attestation signature cannot be delegated below the service's named owner, and that **a vacancy in that role suspends changes rather than the attestation**. If the named owner post is vacant or in handover on the planned apply date, **the change waits** — it does not proceed with a stand-in signatory lined up.

### 6d. Choosing the date

Earliest permissible apply date = the later of:
- 17 business days after the last AN-5 delivery, in the relevant consuming calendars; and
- the first day outside QW-4 for the period in question,

with the named owner in post. Pick a date that also leaves a **full settlement cycle** clear before the attestation is due (Step 8) — the stream settles during the overnight window and its lag is reviewed each morning, so the first full settlement is the night following the apply.

## 7. Apply the change

On the approved date, with all of Step 6 satisfied:

1. Confirm the register entry for the new version is in place and complete (version, RB-7 classification, approver).
2. Confirm QW-4 standing on the finance group's internal page for the current period — re-check on the day, not only at planning time.
3. Deploy the producer so it writes the registered version.
4. Watch the overnight settlement and the morning lag review, per the stream's day-to-day operating pattern.

**The material describes no rollback or back-out procedure for a registered governed-stream version, and no procedure for withdrawing or superseding a register entry.** Do not improvise one silently: reverting the record shape is itself a change to the record shape, which on the face of the Change Class Directory is another RB-7. Establish the back-out path with the tier owner **before** the apply date, not during an incident. See *Open items*.

## 8. Attest — the change is not finished until this is filed

The producing service's owner files **form AT-12** once the change is **live and the first full settlement has passed**.

The form states:

- that the records now flowing **match the registered version**;
- that **no consumer-visible field was dropped** along the way;
- that the **announced scope is the delivered scope**.

Constraints on the signature:

- It is **personal to the owner**. It **cannot be delegated below the service's named owner**.
- A **vacancy in that role suspends changes rather than the attestation** — the attestation still waits for a named owner to sign.
- An **unattested change stays open in the tier's books and is raised at every review** until the form is filed. There is no lapse and no ageing-out.

Before signing, reconcile the AN-5 bulletin text against what actually shipped. If the delivered scope drifted from the announced scope — a different field name, an extra field, a different type — the third clause of AT-12 cannot honestly be signed, and the correct response is to correct the announcement and the register, not the signature.

## 9. Contingency — if the change goes wrong

This branch is genuinely reachable: the Schema Version Register makes an unregistered record shape reaching the stream **an incident** by definition, and `orders-ledger` feeds settlement.

**Severity.** Severity is assigned when the record is opened and **belongs to the standard, not to the team that opened it**. A **reconciliation or settlement control failing across a statement cycle is band SB-8**. SB-8 notifies **the owning team and the platform group's shift lead at opening**, and escalates along the **garnet route**. Single-night failures and non-control degradations carry lighter bands, which notify the owning team only and do not escalate unattended.

**Escalation.** The garnet route climbs **platform shift lead → duty manager → head of platform operations**. An escalation climbs one rung at a time and never skips a rung that has acknowledged. Each rung holds for the acknowledgment clock recorded in the acknowledgment clock table — **that table is not present in this material**, so the hold durations cannot be stated here; see *Open items*.

**Regulatory overlay.** Bands touching settlement controls carry an obligation that is not engineering's to schedule: where the failure falls **inside a statutory filing window**, notification follows the Regulatory Filing Calendar maintained by the compliance office. Filing windows are published a year ahead. Where anything on a filing's in-scope list was **interrupted while the filing was being prepared**, **form RN-26** is lodged with the filing **before the window closes**, stating what was interrupted, the days affected, and the basis on which the filed figures stand. The office **can only lodge what it has been told while the window is open** — word arriving after lodgment becomes a **correction**, which regulators treat differently. Tell compliance immediately, not after the incident is resolved.

**Closure.** A control-failure incident **closes on evidence, not on silence**. Closure requires a **CE-2 evidence record**: the control **passing on its own schedule, unassisted**, with the previously unagreed days **brought current**. A manually forced pass does not qualify — the record must come from the scheduled run itself — and a quiet night with the control disabled qualifies even less. The CE-2 record is attached to the incident **before the closing notice goes out**.

**After closure**, the incident owes a review record, due on its own standard's clock rather than at closure time. **That standard is not present in this material**; see *Open items*.
